scene.note: The book stops being one long text: your functions split it into lines and parts, take the numbers out, and join a line back together.

steps.note: A radio message comes in with spaces wherever someone pressed the bar.
It is cut into words, any run of spaces counting as one gap.
How many words there are comes back, so a long message is spotted.
The book is one text, a line end after each callout, typed on any computer.
It is cut at every line end, whatever kind it is.
A list of lines comes back, no empty line at the end.
One line of the book, spaces around the semicolons wherever they fell.
The line is cut at each semicolon, and each part is tidied.
Every part is still text, the numbers too.
From each line, the hours part is taken, a number with a word after it.
The number is taken out of the text and turned into a whole number.
The hours of every line are added up for Rhona's report.
A line comes in with the hill spelt wrong.
It is split into parts, and the hill's part is swapped for the right name.
The parts are joined back into one line, a semicolon and a space between each.
